sections.h2: Where is Danville, Virginia, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Danville is an independent city in the Southside Virginia region, right on the fall line of the Dan River and against the North Carolina border. It covers about 43 square miles, sits at an elevation of 531 feet, and lies roughly 70 miles south of Lynchburg and 45 miles northeast of Greensboro, North Carolina, by way of U.S. 29.

Because Danville is an independent city, no county government sits between you and city hall. The city bills your real estate tax, and it is bordered by Pittsylvania County on the north and Caswell County, North Carolina, on the south. The Census Bureau counted 42,590 people in 2020 and estimates 41,647 for 2025.

That number is lower than the 53,056 recorded in 1990, and the drop shapes what sellers see. Fewer buyers compete for some older houses, and more houses sit vacant than in faster-growing parts of Virginia.

sections.h2: How did tobacco and textiles shape Danville's housing?
sections.html:
Danville grew around tobacco and cotton mills, and the houses built for that wealth still define many neighborhoods. A tobacco warehouse was authorized at the site in 1793, and the village took the name Danville that same year. Riverside Cotton Mills, later known nationally as Dan River Inc., was founded in 1882 and became the largest single-unit textile mill in the world in its day.

In April 1865 the city briefly served as the last capital of the Confederacy, and the Sutherlin mansion where Jefferson Davis stayed is now the Danville Museum of Fine Arts and History. Late in the twentieth century the tobacco, textile and railroad industries all restructured, and the city lost many jobs.

Preservation Virginia named the entire city one of the Most Endangered Historic Sites in the state in 2007, which tells you how much old building stock Danville has. Older mill-era and Victorian homes can need foundation, plumbing and wiring work that conventional buyers hesitate over.

Danville has several recognized historic districts, and a house inside one of them may carry design expectations that a house elsewhere does not. According to Wikipedia, the recognized districts are the Old West End, Tobacco Warehouse, Downtown Danville, Holbrook-Ross Street and North Main, and the Penn's Bottom stretch of Main Street, the city's first suburb, is also designated.

Millionaire's Row on Main Street has mansions built in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries by tobacco planters. The River District is the revitalized downtown and tobacco warehouse area, where old warehouses have been converted to offices, lofts, apartments and restaurants.

  • Check whether your house sits inside a historic district before you plan exterior changes.
  • Ask the city whether any tax abatement or relief program applies to your parcel.
  • Gather any permits for past renovations, since older houses often have unpermitted work.

These details help a cash buyer decide how much repair a house will need.

Danville's employer list mixes manufacturing, healthcare and a new casino. Wikipedia names these businesses in the city:

Caesars Virginia opened on December 17, 2024, at the site of the old mill, after city voters approved a casino referendum in 2020. Swedwood, an IKEA subsidiary, opened its first U.S. factory in Danville in 2008 and closed it in December 2019, a reminder that employers here can come and go. Averett University and Danville Community College add education jobs.

sections.h2: What are Danville's real estate tax rate and due dates?
sections.html:
The City of Danville lists its real estate tax rate at $0.83 per $100 of assessed value, and bills fall due on December 5 and June 5. Assessment values and rates run from July 1 through June 30 of the following year, so a new year can bring a new rate.

The city's own example shows how it works: a $100,000 assessment times $0.0083 gives $830 a year, billed as two $415 installments. Bills are mailed by November 5 for the first half and by May 5 for the second.

The Real Estate office is at 427 Patton Street, Room 301. Have the parcel ID or the owner's name on the July 1 deed ready when you call, because the staff asks for it. The city also publishes pages on elderly or disabled tax relief, disabled veterans, land use and delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: What do Danville sellers owe at closing?
sections.html:
At closing, Danville sellers settle any unpaid real estate tax and pay Virginia's grantor tax on the deed. Virginia law puts tax liens ahead of other liens, and the lien stays until the city is actually paid. The statute also says the seller's tax liability is prorated by contract, so the sales agreement should state which side covers which period.

The state's grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of the price, and the seller normally pays it unless the two sides agree otherwise. The clerk of court collects the tax when the deed is recorded.

  • Request a payoff for the current half-year installment before closing day.
  • Ask the Division of Central Collections whether delinquent balances show on the parcel.
  • Ask your title company to run a lien and judgment search.
  • Keep copies of any city notices about code or utility charges.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and schools affect a Danville sale?
sections.html:
Danville sits on two major U.S. highways, which makes the city easy to reach for buyers coming from Greensboro or Lynchburg. U.S. 58 runs east and west through the main commercial district, with a bypass along the Danville Expressway, and U.S. 29 runs north and south. U.S. 360 connects the city with Richmond, and the U.S. 29 bypass is planned as future Interstate 785.

Amtrak's Crescent stops at the 1899 station at 677 Craghead Street, and Danville Regional Airport serves general aviation. Public high schools named by Wikipedia include George Washington High School and Galileo Magnet High School, with the Piedmont Governor's School for Mathematics, Science, and Technology also listed. Check the school division directly for current zoning, since boundaries change.

sections.h2: What problems do Danville homeowners face when selling?
sections.html:
Many Danville sellers own a house that is older, vacant or hard to finance. The 2020 census counted 22,259 housing units in the city, and 14.6 percent were vacant, with a rental vacancy rate of 10.7 percent.

  • Inherited houses where the heirs live out of state.
  • Vacant homes that attract code notices and vandalism.
  • Mill-era houses with deferred maintenance and old wiring.
  • Rental properties with tenant turnover or unpaid rent.

A cash sale lets you sell as-is, close on a date you choose and skip showings. We can buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer, and any offer depends on the condition and title of the house. Compare it against listing and choose what fits.

faqs.q: What is the real estate tax rate in Danville, VA?
faqs.a: The City of Danville lists $0.83 per $100 of assessed value. Rates take effect July 1 and run through the following June 30, so check the city's Real Estate Taxes page for the current figure.

faqs.q: When are Danville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due December 5 and June 5. The city mails the first-half bill by November 5 and the second-half bill by May 5.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant or inherited house in Danville?
faqs.a: Yes. Heirs can sell once the person with authority signs the deed, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is. Confirm the legal authority with an attorney or title company before signing.

faqs.q: Does Virginia charge a transfer tax on the seller?
faqs.a: Virginia imposes a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the sale price on the deed. The seller usually pays it, though the contract can shift some or all of it to the buyer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Danville real estate tax amounts?
faqs.a: Call the Division of Central Collections at 434-799-5125, or the Real Estate office at 434-799-5120. Have the parcel ID, address or tax bill in front of you.
No. Danville is an independent city, so the city itself assesses and bills real estate tax. Pittsylvania County lies to the north.
